scope: Six operative AGENTS plus current controller/README. Frozen experiment copies excluded from current-rule recommendations.
decision: Targeted AGENTS edits are justified. One thin workflow-orchestrator skill is worth a bounded trial but is optional; no measured efficacy claim.

graph_evidence.search_and_coverage: project not found or not indexed
graph_evidence.fallback: Direct reads of all six operative AGENTS, contracts.py, loop.py and README; no graph completeness claim.

findings.claim: Some nested field types and enum values remain implicit in role docs although the controller enforces them.

evidence.observation: validation_results[].required is named without its boolean type.
failure_modes[].likely_stage is named without enumerating allowed values.
likely_stage must be one of STAGES.
conflicts[].blocks_execution is named without an explicit boolean type.

findings.recommendation: Complete nested types/enums and maintain a doc-controller consistency check. The planner array issue is already explicitly fixed; do not describe it as still broken.

findings.claim: Fresh invocation is the stated isolation goal; main-owned same-invocation execution is a limited fallback. These are different evidence modes, not an established rule contradiction.

evidence.observation: Outer authorization must carry scoped exceptions.

findings.recommendation: Explain how the fallback operates under the human only-opposition restriction and record actual execution mode. Preserve the original isolation goal for all tasks; do not limit it to experiments or reuse the prior Luna exception.

findings.claim: Orchestrator duties already exist but are distributed between root rules and CLI README.

evidence.observation: Report actual validation exit/digest outside artifact and recheck routing.
Dispatch prepares message/metadata, never launches agent.

findings.recommendation: Add a short orchestrator entrypoint referencing existing operations and owners. A mandatory receipt location would be new policy, not a repair of a missing existing requirement.

findings.claim: All tasks currently require five stages, including this bounded cleanup/assessment.

evidence.observation: All tasks MUST use full pipeline.

findings.recommendation: If administrative overhead becomes a concern, explicitly decide whether pure questions or maintenance need a lighter mode. Keep all five stages until the user approves any policy change.

keep: Scoped outer authorization and human provenance boundary
Review mirrors and cross-stage required checks
Structured blockers and earliest supported failure attribution
Schema/hash agreement is not proof of semantics or actual execution

skill_proposal.name: workflow-orchestrator
skill_proposal.necessity: Optional operating aid, not required for controller correctness.
skill_proposal.trigger: Operating or resuming this repository workflow and preparing review; no blanket trigger for unrelated coding.
contents: Locate operative root/stage rules and task requirements.
Check current route and capture fresh input metadata using existing CLI.
Carry verified authority in every actual fresh dispatch; no new permission created by the skill.
Guide save, validate actual bytes, report exit/digest, prepare review mirrors and recheck route.
On stale input, reread/reproduce affected stages; do not replace hashes or blindly retry side effects.
boundaries: Do not copy the five schemas or create five role skills.
Keep authoritative task requirements and task-specific validation/cleanup/rollback in task files.
Reference existing reusable CLI/playbooks; root AGENTS already permits project resources referenced by tasks.
Do not claim isolation, truthful execution or improved model success from skill presence.
trial_acceptance: Correct routing under valid, malformed, stale and blocked inputs.
No reuse of another task authorization exception.
No claimed fresh invocation for same-conversation fallback.
Compare with the same existing CLI workflow before making efficacy claims.

counterargument_disposition: Accepted: orchestrator mechanisms already exist; describe consolidation, not absence.
Accepted: fallback is not permission to redefine all normal tasks as non-isolated.
Accepted: no current concrete stage/root precedence conflict established; no mandatory precedence rewrite recommended.
Accepted: skill utility remains a hypothesis; preserve task authority and avoid duplicated runbooks.
limits: No rules, skill, controller or frozen experiments changed.
No new model experiment or efficacy measurement.
Graph unavailable; bounded direct-source assessment only.
This task used the main-agent same-invocation fallback.
orchestration_correction: Initial helper mistakenly parsed the text output of next as JSON after tasker validation. Corrected to inspect its documented first-line decision; validated tasker bytes were unchanged, and no deletion or later stage ran before a successful route check.
